info.title: Chasha Platform API
info.summary: Official REST API Documentation for Chasha Platform
info.description:
The official REST API powering the Chasha Restaurant Operating System.

This API enables platform administration, restaurant management, authentication, ordering, QR menu, kitchen workflow, notifications, and future platform services.

All endpoints follow REST principles and return standardized JSON responses.

Authentication supports both Cookie-based and Bearer Token authorization depending on client platform.

post.description:
Starts the Platform Administrator authentication process.

This endpoint validates the administrator credentials (phone number and password).

If the credentials are valid:
- Creates a temporary login session.
- Generates a six-digit OTP.
- Stores the session in cache.
- Returns a temporary loginSession identifier.

The returned loginSession must be used during OTP verification.

If there is already an active login session for this phone number, the API returns an error asking the client to continue the existing verification process instead of creating a new one.

400.description: Validation failed or business rule violation.

loginPhoneNumber: Phone number must contain exactly 11 digits and start with 09.

error_message: Your login request is already in progress. Please return to the verification page and enter your OTP.

loginPhoneNumber: Platform administrator with this phone number does not exist.

post.description:
Completes the Platform Administrator authentication process.

This endpoint validates the temporary login session and verifies the one-time password (OTP).

Verification flow:

1. Validates request body.
2. Finds temporary login session.
3. Checks session expiration.
4. Validates OTP.
5. Finds Platform Administrator.
6. Creates a permanent authenticated session.
7. Generates JWT Access Token.
8. Generates JWT Refresh Token.
9. Stores hashed Refresh Token inside Platform Admin Session.
10. Deletes temporary login cache.

Client behavior:

• Web Client:
- Access Token is returned as HttpOnly Cookie.
- Refresh Token is returned as HttpOnly Cookie.
- Response data is null.

• Mobile Client:
- Access Token is returned inside response body.
- Refresh Token is returned inside response body.

The client platform is determined using the 'x-platform' request header.

Accepted values:
- web
- mobile

Set-Cookie.description: Only returned for Web platform. Contains Access Token and Refresh Token as HttpOnly cookies.

loginVerifySessionId: Session identifier must be a valid UUID.

404.description: Session or Platform Administrator not found.

loginVerifyPhoneNumber: Login session has expired or does not exist.

post.description:
Generates a new OTP for an existing Platform Administrator login session.

This endpoint is used when the previous OTP has expired.

Flow:

1. Validates phone number and session identifier.
2. Finds existing temporary login session.
3. Checks session ownership.
4. Validates previous OTP expiration.
5. Generates a new six-digit OTP.
6. Updates login session cache.
7. Returns new OTP expiration timer.

The existing loginSession identifier remains unchanged and must continue to be used for OTP verification.

400.description: Validation failed or OTP is still valid.

post.description:
Generates new authentication tokens for a Platform Administrator using the refresh token stored in HttpOnly Cookie.

Refresh token lifecycle:

1. Reads refresh token from HttpOnly Cookie.
2. Validates refresh token signature.
3. Checks token ownership.
4. Finds Platform Administrator session.
5. Validates session expiration.
6. Compares stored hashed refresh token.
7. Rotates refresh token.
8. Updates session activity and expiration time.
9. Sets new Access Token and Refresh Token as HttpOnly Cookies.

The response body does not contain authentication tokens.

Set-Cookie.description: New Access Token and Refresh Token are returned as HttpOnly cookies.

401.description: Refresh token is invalid, expired, or session is not valid.

error_message: Refresh token is invalid or has expired.

get.summary: Check current platform administrator authentication status
get.description:
Checks whether the current request belongs to an authenticated Platform Administrator.

This endpoint is used by frontend applications during initialization to restore authentication state.

The endpoint does not return administrator information. It only validates:

- Access Token validity.
- Platform Administrator session existence.
- Session active status.
- Session expiration time.

Authentication is performed using HttpOnly Cookie or Bearer Token.

401.description: Authentication failed because access token or session is invalid.

error_message: Access token is invalid or session has expired.

post.description:
Terminates the current authenticated Platform Administrator session.

The endpoint requires an active authentication session validated by authentication middleware.

Logout flow:

1. Validates current Access Token.
2. Identifies authenticated Platform Administrator session from authentication middleware.
3. Retrieves session identifier from authentication context.
4. Revokes the active authentication session.
5. Invalidates the refresh token to prevent future token usage.
6. Clears authentication cookies for Web clients.

For mobile clients, the backend revokes the session. The client application is responsible for removing locally stored tokens from Secure Storage.

Set-Cookie.description: Authentication cookies are cleared for Web clients.

401.description: Authentication failed because access token or session is invalid.

error_message: Access token is invalid or authentication session has expired.

post.summary: Login business employee with phone number
post.description:
Starts authentication process for business employees.

This endpoint validates business employee credentials using phone number and password.

If credentials are valid:
- Generates access token.
- Generates refresh token.
- Creates authenticated session.
- Returns tokens based on client platform.

For web clients, tokens are stored in HttpOnly cookies.
For mobile clients, tokens are returned in response body.

loginPhoneNumber: Business employee with this phone number does not exist.

post.description:
Generates new access and refresh tokens for an authenticated business employee without requiring login again.

Refresh token lifecycle:

1. Validates refresh token signature.
2. Checks token type ownership.
3. Finds existing business employee session.
4. Validates stored hashed refresh token.
5. Rotates refresh token.
6. Updates session activity and expiration time.
7. Returns new authentication tokens.

The previous refresh token becomes invalid after rotation.

401.description: Refresh token is invalid or expired.

post.description:
Initiates the password reset process for a business employee using their phone number.

For security reasons, this endpoint does not reveal whether the provided phone number belongs to an existing business employee.

If a business employee exists with the provided phone number:
- A temporary password reset session is created in cache.
- A password reset verification code is generated.
- The verification code is sent to the employee via SMS.

If no business employee exists with the provided phone number, no password reset session or SMS is created.

In both cases, the API returns the same successful response to prevent user enumeration.

200.description: Password reset request processed successfully. The response is intentionally identical whether or not the phone number belongs to a business employee.

forgotPasswordPhoneNumber: Phone number must contain exactly 11 digits and start with 09.

post.description:
Completes the password reset process for a business employee.

This endpoint validates the password reset token, verifies the associated password reset session, updates the employee password, revokes all active authentication sessions for the employee, and invalidates the password reset session.

Password reset flow:

1. Validates the reset token and new password.
2. Hashes the reset token and locates the temporary password reset session.
3. Validates that the password reset session is still active.
4. Verifies that the business employee exists.
5. Updates the business employee password.
6. Revokes all active authentication sessions belonging to the employee.
7. Deletes the password reset session from cache.

After successful completion, the business employee must authenticate again using the new password.

400.description: Validation failed or password reset session is invalid.

forgotPasswordVerifyResetToken: Password reset session is invalid or has expired.
Password reset session is invalid or has expired.

post.description:
Creates a new Early Access request for businesses interested in joining the Chasha platform.

This endpoint is publicly accessible and does not require authentication.

If the phone number has already been registered, the API returns a conflict error.

earlyAccessRequestPhoneNumber: Phone number must contain exactly 11 digits and start with 09.

earlyAccessRequestPhoneNumber: An Early Access request has already been submitted for this phone number.

get.summary: Get Early Access Request list options
get.description: Retrieves the available search fields and status filter options for the Platform Administrator Early Access Request management interface. This endpoint is protected by Platform Administrator authentication and requires the EARLY_ACCESS_REQUEST_LIST_OPTIONS permission.

200.description: Early Access Request list options retrieved successfully.

get.description: Retrieves a paginated list of Early Access Requests for Platform Administrators. The endpoint supports pagination, global search, and status filtering. Search is performed across the Early Access Request full name, phone number, business name, and request code. The query schema is strict and unsupported query parameters are rejected. This endpoint is protected by Platform Administrator authentication and requires the EARLY_ACCESS_REQUEST_GET_ALL permission.

This endpoint is publicly accessible and does not require authentication.
